These examples fit joint models and use gratia to draw their smooths and
check each response distribution. Run
`Rscript notes/gjrm-support/render-examples.R` from this package checkout
to reproduce the HTML report, R examples, fitted models and PNG figures.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library("gratia")
  library("mgcv")
  library("ggplot2")
  library("patchwork")
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
  fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8, dpi = 140,
  dev = "png", fig.path = "figures/"
)
options(width = 90)
```

## Two Gaussian responses, including random effects

The first response has a smooth effect of `x` and a group effect. The second
has a smooth effect of `z` and a standard deviation that changes with `x`.
The dependence between the responses changes with `z`.

```{r gaussian-data}
set.seed(510)
n <- 360
d <- data.frame(
  x = runif(n), z = runif(n),
  group = factor(rep(letters[1:12], each = 30))
)
group_effect <- rnorm(12, sd = 0.35)
mu1 <- sin(2 * pi * d$x) + group_effect[d$group]
mu2 <- 0.5 + cos(2 * pi * d$z)
sd1 <- 0.7
sd2 <- exp(-0.3 + 0.4 * d$x)
rho <- 0.2 + 0.45 * d$z
e1 <- rnorm(n)
e2 <- rho * e1 + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * rnorm(n)
d$y1 <- mu1 + sd1 * e1
d$y2 <- mu2 + sd2 * e2
```

The formulas describe the two means, two standard deviations and the
dependence parameter, in that order.

```{r gaussian-fit}
set.seed(511)
joint_normal <- GJRM::gjrm(
  list(
    y1 ~ s(x, k = 7) + s(group, bs = "re"),
    y2 ~ s(z, k = 7), ~ 1,
    ~ s(x, k = 5), ~ s(z, k = 5)
  ),
  data = d, margins = c("N", "N"), model = "B"
)
smooths(joint_normal)
```

`draw()` uses the same smooth and random-effect plots as it does for a GAM.

```{r gaussian-smooths, fig.height=11}
normal_smooth_plot <- draw(joint_normal, ncol = 2, n = 100)
normal_smooth_plot
```

`assemble()` returns individual plots. Here is the random effect on its own.

```{r gaussian-random-effect, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
normal_panels <- assemble(joint_normal, parametric = FALSE)
normal_panels[[2]]
```

### Saved smooth estimates and selection

Smooth labels identify terms across all equations. Repeated labels receive
distinct suffixes. The last label below selects the dependence smooth.

```{r saved-estimates}
dependence_label <- tail(smooths(joint_normal), 1)
dependence <- smooth_estimates(joint_normal, select = dependence_label, n = 80)
head(dependence[c(".smooth", ".estimate", ".se", "z", ".model")])
```

```{r saved-estimate-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
draw(dependence)
```

### Four diagnostic panels, each separated by response

`appraise()` produces one QQ plot, residual-versus-predictor plot, histogram,
and observed-versus-fitted plot. Every panel has a facet for each response.
These diagnostics check each response distribution; they do not check the
copula that links the responses.

```{r gaussian-appraisal, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
normal_appraisal <- appraise(joint_normal, seed = 512, ncol = 2)
normal_appraisal
```

Select a single response when its diagnostics need a closer look.

```{r gaussian-response-two, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
appraise(joint_normal, response = 2, seed = 512, ncol = 2)
```

## A binary response and a lognormal response

Both responses are observed for every row. The first is binary and uses a
probit link. The second is positive and lognormal. Its observed-versus-fitted
plot uses the expected response on its original scale, including the
contribution of the lognormal standard deviation.

```{r mixed-data}
set.seed(520)
mixed <- data.frame(x = runif(400), z = runif(400))
a <- rnorm(nrow(mixed))
b <- 0.45 * a + sqrt(1 - 0.45^2) * rnorm(nrow(mixed))
mixed$present <- as.integer(0.1 + sin(2 * pi * mixed$x) + a > 0)
mixed$duration <- exp(0.4 + 0.6 * cos(2 * pi * mixed$z) + 0.45 * b)
```

```{r mixed-fit}
set.seed(521)
joint_mixed <- GJRM::gjrm(
  list(
    present ~ s(x, k = 7), duration ~ s(z, k = 7),
    ~ 1, ~ s(x, k = 5)
  ),
  data = mixed, margins = c("probit", "LN"), model = "B"
)
```

```{r mixed-smooths}
draw(joint_mixed, ncol = 2)
```

```{r mixed-appraisal, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
appraise(joint_mixed, seed = 522, ncol = 2)
```

Standalone diagnostics retain the same response grouping. A worm plot shows
the departures from the QQ reference.

```{r mixed-worm, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
worm_plot(joint_mixed, seed = 522)
```

PIT residuals are returned as a matrix with one column per response. Selecting
one response returns a vector.

```{r mixed-residuals}
pit <- quantile_residuals(joint_mixed, type = "pit", seed = 522)
head(pit)
pit_duration <- quantile_residuals(
  joint_mixed, type = "pit", response = 2, seed = 522
)
head(pit_duration)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(pit[, 2]), unname(pit_duration))))
```

## A count response and a Gaussian response

The count has a negative-binomial margin. Here `NBI` uses
\(\operatorname{Var}(Y)=\mu+\sigma\mu^2\).
The two responses share correlated errors.

```{r count-data}
set.seed(530)
counts <- data.frame(x = runif(360), z = runif(360))
a <- rnorm(nrow(counts))
b <- 0.4 * a + sqrt(1 - 0.4^2) * rnorm(nrow(counts))
counts$count <- qnbinom(
  pnorm(a), mu = exp(0.8 + 0.6 * sin(2 * pi * counts$x)), size = 3
)
counts$value <- cos(2 * pi * counts$z) + 0.8 * b
```

```{r count-fit}
set.seed(531)
joint_count <- GJRM::gjrm(
  list(
    count ~ s(x, k = 7), value ~ s(z, k = 7),
    ~ 1, ~ 1, ~ s(x, k = 5)
  ),
  data = counts, margins = c("NBI", "N"), model = "B"
)
```

```{r count-smooths}
draw(joint_count, ncol = 2)
```

```{r count-appraisal, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
appraise(joint_count, seed = 532, ncol = 2)
```

The scalable version summarizes the point clouds while keeping the responses
separate.

```{r count-scalable, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
appraise(joint_count, seed = 532, scalable = TRUE, ncol = 2)
```

## Factor-by smooths in both responses

Each response has a separate curve for each level of `f`. Grouped plots
keep those curves together within their response. Parametric factor effects
also identify which response they belong to.

```{r factor-by-fit}
set.seed(535)
by_data <- data.frame(x = runif(360),
  f = factor(rep(c("a", "b"), each = 180)))
a <- rnorm(nrow(by_data))
b <- 0.3 * a + sqrt(1 - 0.3^2) * rnorm(nrow(by_data))
by_data$y1 <- ifelse(by_data$f == "a", 1, 0.5) *
  sin(2 * pi * by_data$x) + 0.4 * (by_data$f == "b") + 0.45 * a
by_data$y2 <- ifelse(by_data$f == "a", 1, -1) *
  cos(2 * pi * by_data$x) + 0.2 * (by_data$f == "a") + 0.45 * b
set.seed(536)
joint_by <- GJRM::gjrm(
  list(y1 ~ f + s(x, by = f, k = 7),
    y2 ~ f + s(x, by = f, k = 7)),
  data = by_data, margins = c("N", "N"), model = "B"
)
names(assemble(joint_by, grouped_by = TRUE))
```

```{r factor-by-smooths}
draw(joint_by, grouped_by = TRUE, ncol = 2)
```

Saved estimates contain smooths only. Their grouped plots retain the response
identities and fitted term order.

```{r factor-by-saved, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
by_estimates <- smooth_estimates(joint_by)
draw(by_estimates, grouped_by = TRUE, ncol = 2)
```

## A two-dimensional smooth

A joint-model tensor smooth uses the existing surface plotting methods.
Estimates saved by `smooth_estimates()` retain the information needed to
draw the surface later.

```{r tensor-fit}
set.seed(540)
joint_tensor <- GJRM::gjrm(
  list(
    y1 ~ te(x, z, k = c(5, 5)) + s(group, bs = "re"),
    y2 ~ s(z, k = 7)
  ),
  data = d, margins = c("N", "N"), model = "B"
)
tensor_values <- smooth_estimates(joint_tensor, select = 1, n_2d = 35)
```

```{r tensor-surface, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
draw(tensor_values)
```

Requesting `scales = "fixed"` gives the plotted effects a common range.
The surface keeps its covariate axes; its fill scale shares the effect range
used by the one-dimensional plots.

```{r tensor-fixed-scales, fig.height=10}
draw(joint_tensor, scales = "fixed", parametric = FALSE, ncol = 2)
```

## An ordinal response

Ordinal models include cutpoints as well as regression coefficients.
Smooth plots use the regression coefficients and exclude cutpoint uncertainty
from the smooth intervals. Appraisal of ordinal margins is not yet supported.

```{r ordinal-fit}
ordinal <- d
ordinal$category <- as.integer(cut(ordinal$y1, c(-Inf, -0.5, 0.5, Inf)))
set.seed(550)
joint_ordinal <- GJRM::gjrm(
  list(
    category ~ s(x, k = 7), y2 ~ s(z, k = 7),
    ~ 1, ~ s(x, k = 5)
  ),
  data = ordinal, margins = c("ord.probit", "N"), model = "B"
)
```

```{r ordinal-smooths}
draw(joint_ordinal, ncol = 2)
```

## Fixed margins: draw the dependence equation

When the marginal distributions are supplied as probabilities, only the
dependence equation is estimated. `draw()` plots that equation.

```{r fixed-fit}
uniforms <- data.frame(
  u1 = pnorm((d$y1 - mu1) / sd1),
  u2 = pnorm((d$y2 - mu2) / sd2),
  z = d$z
)
set.seed(560)
joint_fixed <- GJRM::gjrm(
  list(u1 ~ 1, u2 ~ 1, ~ s(z, k = 6)),
  data = uniforms, margins = c("N", "N"), model = "B",
  fixed.margins = TRUE
)
```

```{r fixed-smooth, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
draw(joint_fixed)
```

## The same response selector for grouped-family GAMs

For a model fitted with `mgcv::gfam()`, `response` refers to the integer
position in its family list. Selecting a component retains its observations.
The `by_family` argument continues to control pooling and faceting
independently.

```{r gfam-response-fit}
set.seed(560)
grouped_data <- data.frame(x = runif(240), family_id = rep(1:3, 80))
grouped_data$component <- factor(grouped_data$family_id)
grouped_data$y <- numeric(nrow(grouped_data))
i <- grouped_data$family_id == 1L
grouped_data$y[i] <- rbinom(sum(i), 1,
  plogis(0.3 + sin(2 * pi * grouped_data$x[i])))
i <- grouped_data$family_id == 2L
grouped_data$y[i] <- 0.5 + cos(2 * pi * grouped_data$x[i]) +
  rnorm(sum(i), sd = 0.4)
i <- grouped_data$family_id == 3L
grouped_data$y[i] <- rpois(sum(i),
  exp(0.2 + 0.5 * sin(2 * pi * grouped_data$x[i])))
grouped_fit <- gam(
  cbind(y, family_id) ~ component + s(x, by = component, k = 6),
  data = grouped_data, method = "REML",
  family = gfam(list(binomial(), gaussian(), poisson()))
)
```

The default `response = NULL` includes every indexed component. This call
requests family facets for the residual panels.

```{r gfam-all-responses, fig.width=15, fig.height=10}
appraise(grouped_fit, by_family = TRUE, seed = 561, ncol = 2)
```

Index 2 selects the Gaussian component and its 80 observations.

```{r gfam-selected-response, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
appraise(grouped_fit, response = 2, seed = 561, ncol = 2)
```

Selection and layout can also be combined in standalone plots. Both QQ plots
below use component 3; only the second asks for a family facet.

```{r gfam-independent-layout, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
qq_plot(grouped_fit, response = 3, by_family = FALSE, seed = 561) +
  qq_plot(grouped_fit, response = 3, by_family = TRUE, seed = 561)
```

Scalable diagnostics accept the same selection.

```{r gfam-selected-scalable, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
scalable_residuals_linpred_plot(grouped_fit, response = 2,
  by_family = TRUE, seed = 561, density_bins = c(12, 40))
```

With the same seed, selected PIT residuals match the corresponding rows
from an all-component call.

```{r gfam-selected-residuals}
grouped_pit <- quantile_residuals(grouped_fit, type = "pit", seed = 561)
poisson_pit <- quantile_residuals(grouped_fit, type = "pit",
  response = 3, seed = 561)
stopifnot(length(poisson_pit) == sum(grouped_data$family_id == 3L),
  isTRUE(all.equal(unname(poisson_pit),
    unname(grouped_pit[grouped_data$family_id == 3L]))))
head(poisson_pit)
```

```{r save-gfam-model, include=FALSE}
saveRDS(grouped_fit, "gfam-example-model.rds")
```

## Fitted objects and versions

The rendering script saves the seven joint fits in `gjrm-example-models.rds` so they
can be inspected without refitting. The grouped-family fit is saved separately in `gfam-example-model.rds`.

```{r save-models, include=FALSE}
example_models <- list(
  gaussian = joint_normal, binary_lognormal = joint_mixed,
  count_gaussian = joint_count, factor_by = joint_by, tensor = joint_tensor,
  ordinal = joint_ordinal, fixed_margins = joint_fixed
)
saveRDS(example_models, "gjrm-example-models.rds")
```

### Numerical checks of the example smooths

The table compares smooth estimates and standard errors with direct products
of the fitted basis matrices and the final joint coefficients and covariance.
These checks use `overall_uncertainty = FALSE` to isolate each smooth's
coefficient block. The plots above retain their usual interval defaults.

```{r coefficient-checks, echo=FALSE, error=FALSE}
withCallingHandlers({
  source("check-smooths.R", local = TRUE)
  expected_smooths <- c(gaussian = 5L, binary_lognormal = 3L,
    count_gaussian = 3L, factor_by = 4L, tensor = 3L,
    ordinal = 3L, fixed_margins = 1L)
  coefficient_check_details <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(fit, name) {
    cbind(model = name, check_example_smooths(fit))
  }, example_models, names(example_models)))
  rownames(coefficient_check_details) <- NULL
  checked_counts <- table(factor(coefficient_check_details$model,
    levels = names(expected_smooths)))
  stopifnot(identical(as.integer(checked_counts), unname(expected_smooths)),
    nrow(coefficient_check_details) == 22L,
    all(coefficient_check_details$evaluation_rows > 0L))
  coefficient_checks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(example_models), function(name) {
    values <- coefficient_check_details[coefficient_check_details$model == name, ]
    data.frame(smooths = nrow(values),
      evaluation_rows = sum(values$evaluation_rows),
      estimate_error = max(values$estimate_error),
      standard_error_error = max(values$standard_error_error))
  }))
  rownames(coefficient_checks) <- names(example_models)
  write.csv(coefficient_checks, "coefficient-checks.csv")
  write.csv(coefficient_check_details, "coefficient-check-details.csv",
    row.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(coefficient_checks, digits = 14)
}, warning = function(w) {
  stop("Numerical checks raised a warning: ", conditionMessage(w), call. = FALSE)
})
```

All **`r nrow(coefficient_check_details)` smooths** were checked across
**`r format(sum(coefficient_check_details$evaluation_rows), big.mark = ",")`
evaluation rows**. Each comparison requires nonempty results with matching
dimensions and finite estimates and standard errors. An unexpected warning
stops the report. The [individual comparisons](coefficient-check-details.csv)
record the equation, smooth and evaluated row count.

```{r versions}
data.frame(
  package = c("gratia", "GJRM", "mgcv"),
  version = vapply(c("gratia", "GJRM", "mgcv"),
    function(x) as.character(packageVersion(x)), character(1))
)
```
